tip: This = 'den här' plus the noun in its definite form: 'den här veckan' = this week.
'Det tar' plus a time plus 'att' plus a verb = it takes that long to: 'tar tre timmar att köra'.
'Att' = that, linking the thought to 'tror': 'tror att det blir regn'.
Yes/no questions put the verb first: 'borde vi inte vänta?' = Shouldn't we wait?
'Tycker om' = like; the 'om' is fixed and cannot be dropped: 'tycker om att promenera'.
'Närmaste' = nearest; the '-aste' ending works like English -est: 'närmaste tunnelbanestation'.
'På' plus a plural weekday means every one: 'på lördagar' = on Saturdays, every Saturday.
Swedish has no word for of here: 'en kopp te' = a cup of tea, just place the words together.
'Lär ha' = is said to have – a way to report unconfirmed information.
'Härifrån' = from here, combining 'här' (here) and 'ifrån' (from): 'busshållplats härifrån'.
'Vår' becomes 'våra' before a plural noun: 'våra föräldrar' = our parents.
The time unit adds '-s' in measurements: 'fem minuters promenad' = a five-minute walk.
'Framme' means arrived/there: 'var vi framme' = we had arrived.
Many 'en'-words add '-ar' in the plural: 'en hund', 'två hundar'.
Adjectives normally add '-a' when the subject is plural: 'barnen är trötta'.
Here 'i' marks how long something lasts: 'i minst en timme' = for at least an hour.
Plural nouns in '-or' end in '-orna' when definite: 'blommor' becomes 'blommorna' = the flowers.
'Ska' plus a verb expresses the future: 'vad ska du göra' = what will you do.
'Gånger i veckan' = times per week: 'fyra gånger i veckan' = four times a week.
Many regular verbs form the past with '-ade': 'ritar' becomes 'ritade' = drew.
'Van vid' = used to; keep 'vid' before 'att': 'van vid att arbeta'.
'Gärna' adds a willing, glad tone to a verb: 'vill gärna prova' = would love to try.
'Hur är läget' is a casual how is it going; 'läget' literally means the situation.
'I veckan' means per week: 'sex dagar i veckan' = six days a week.
'Vänta på' = wait for; the 'på' is required: 'väntade på mig'.
Swedish often picks a position verb for location; things lying flat use 'ligger': 'segelbåten ligger i hamnen'.
'Vakna' is both the base verb and the command; verbs whose base ends in '-a' keep that same '-a' as a command: 'vakna' = wake up.
Most 'en'-words build the plural with '-ar': 'en granne' becomes 'grannar'. The final '-e' drops before the ending.
Nouns ending in '-are' stay identical in the plural: 'invånare' is both one inhabitant and many. Nothing is added.
Definite 'en'-words add '-en' to the noun instead of a separate word for 'the': 'buss' becomes 'bussen' (the bus).
